cards.title: AMP1: Generalist AI Agent Beats Specialist VLA/WAM Policies on Robot Manipulation Benchmarks
cards.why_it_matters: This directly challenges the dominant VLA/world-model paradigm in robot manipulation — a result every robotics and embodied-AI researcher needs to know.
cards.summary: AMP1, a generalist-AI-based agentic manipulation policy, achieves 85.6% zero-shot success on RoboLab-120 vs. 49.2% for the leading VLA and 42.9% for the leading WAM. In 108 real-world trials it cuts failure rates 20x and 15x vs. those baselines. Adding a persistent memory store reduces failure on RoboDojo bimanual tasks by 4.6x over zero-shot.

cards.title: CPU-ARC: Cache LLM Reasoning Traces as CPU-Executable Programs for 16–291x Cost Reduction
cards.why_it_matters: Separating reasoning from execution is a compelling systems insight with direct implications for inference cost and continual learning in deployed AI agents.
cards.summary: CPU-ARC extracts agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) from LLM reasoning traces, compiling them into CPU-executable programs that can be reused across problem instances without re-invoking the source model. ARCs match frontier LLM performance on hard math and science tasks while being 16–291x cheaper to invoke, and are fully explainable, robust to input perturbations, and continually trainable.

cards.title: FlowMoP: Conditional Flow Matching for Stochastic Multi-Person 3D Motion Prediction
cards.why_it_matters: Replacing deterministic multi-agent motion prediction with a principled generative framework is relevant to anyone working on world models, simulation, or social robotics.
cards.summary: FlowMoP uses conditional flow matching to jointly generate diverse future motions for multiple agents, combining global trajectory and root-relative pose modeling. A B-spline reparameterization enforces temporal smoothness and compresses the state space; a dual-stream transformer provides interaction-aware conditioning. The method achieves state-of-the-art on CMU-Mocap (UMPM) and 3DPW on joint position, pose, and final displacement error, and establishes the first motion-prediction baseline on the WorldPose soccer dataset.

cards.title: ReLU Networks with One Hidden Layer Are Weakly Closed; Two Hidden Layers Are Not
cards.why_it_matters: Settling the topological structure of ReLU function spaces has direct consequences for the theoretical guarantees of training methods like Deep Ritz, Sobolev training, and Lipschitz learning.
cards.summary: The paper proves that the set of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with at most N neurons is weakly closed in W^{1,p}, guaranteeing that coercive weakly lower-semicontinuous energies attain minima there, and that regularized minimizers converge to minimal-norm solutions as weight decay vanishes. It also disproves a conjecture by Petersen, Raslan, and Voigtlaender by showing two-hidden-layer networks of bounded width are not closed in W^{1,p} or C.

cards.title: Graded Convolutional Networks: Scale-Invariant, Blur-Robust Vision Without Knowing the Scale
cards.why_it_matters: A principled geometric solution to blur and scale invariance — grounded in differential geometry — offers a theoretically clean alternative to ad-hoc data augmentation for robust vision models.
cards.summary: The paper formalizes dilation invariance via retraction onto the weighted sphere of the Gaussian jet's graded structure, showing this retraction changes only by a scale factor under unknown Gaussian blur — unlike scale-normalized jets which acquire an irremovable grading factor. On MNIST under two-pixel blur, a network using the retraction achieves 88.4% accuracy vs. 66.2% for scale-normalized derivatives; applied to Lindeberg's Gaussian derivative network, the retraction raises accuracy from 91.5% to 95.1%.
